report: Source reassessment: the complete claim requires (1) stable semantic products as query boundaries, (2) semantic keys for every public tracked query, (3) the narrowest independently reusable product for each key, and (4) temporary algorithm state remaining within its owning query instead of separately memoized public substeps. The sole implementation association is an explicit TODO in service_spec.rs: the full public-boundary audit and per-product dependency guarantees remain incomplete. The sole associated test, sage_meta::todo::crates_sage_ir_crate_semantic_query_boundaries, is an empty TODO body, not executable behavioral evidence. Its comments require representative phase/subsystem key/result and permitted/forbidden dependency declarations and traces excluding unrelated products and separately public temporary substeps. Together these explicitly defer all four aspects; no implemented or N/A evidence is claimed. Prerequisites are completing the public tracked-query inventory and semantic key/product audit (including minimal independent reuse), defining per-product dependency contracts, and associating assertion-bearing demand-trace tests that enforce those contracts and algorithm-state locality. The existing TODO accounting is adequate and remains deferred. Baseline verification: personally compared both historical whole-file source snapshots against current service_spec.rs bytes, with exact matches; claim and implementation metadata also match. Historical test metadata differs only by its legacy inline source field, whose body is present in the current captured test fragment. Reassessed the supplied historical rationale against the full current captured source and associated test; acceptance is of explicit deferral, not completed coverage. Execution: ran review start and baseline comparison scripts; no behavioral tests or build were run by this reviewer. The coordinator reports 321 passing sage-meta tests and a passing root build, which are separate reported execution and do not establish this deferred claim. No additional implementation dependencies were used.
